column13: First part of this day thick overcast weather & moderate breeze from the northwest. Ship steering S.W. by W. under all sail until 3 o’clock. Wind hauled to the S.W. Took in all sail except close-reefed maintopsail & foresail. Became fresh from the southward. Middle part quite pleasant. Latter part pleasant, with moderate breeze from the southward. Ship steering W. by N. under all sail. In night saw nothing of note this day.

column12: The ship sailed close to the wind before conditions became calm; grampuses and porpoises were sighted, but no whales.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the southward. Ship steering to the wind under all sail, heading west. Saw nothing of note. Middle part calm. Latter part much the same. Saw grampuses & porpoises, but no whales.

column12: Porpoises were abundant and the crew performed ship duty; a fresh breeze and rain developed later.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate calm. Saw plenty of porpoises. Employed in ship duty. Middle part moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering S.W. by S.E. Latter part fresh breeze from the S.E. Rainy, pleasant. Saw nothing of note.

column12: The final coordinate line is difficult to read.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & strong breezes from the N.E. Ship steering S.W. by S. under topsail, courses & jib. Ship in sight. Employed in ship's duty. William Jackson, a seaman, off duty sick with the venereal disease & has been afflicted for 8 days. Middle part pleasant with strong breezes from the S.E. Ship steering by the wind heading S.W. under topsail & courses. Latter part more moderate; set mainsail, spanker & sail. Wind S. by E. Ship heading W. by S. by the wind.

column12: The wind strengthened through the day; topgallant sails were struck and two porpoises were caught.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & light wind from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. by S. under all sail. Middle part moderate winds from the N.W., steering S.W. by S. Latter part strong W.S.W. breezes, steering the same. Struck topgallant sails. Saw porpoises & caught 2.

column8: S. by E.; S.W. by W.
column12: The ship initially sailed close to the wind under topsails and courses, then made all sail; crew performed ship duty.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breezes from the northward. Ship steering by the wind, heading S. by E., under topsails & courses. Middle part pleasant. Wind W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. by W. under all sail. Latter part the same. Saw porpoises & swordfish. Employed in ship duty.

column12: The fore and mizzen topgallant sails and spanker were furled; fog and light winds were followed by calm conditions. The entry ends with “Saw several” without identifying what was seen.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & strong breeze from the W.S.W. Ship steering S.W. by S. At 3 o’clock furled fore & mizzen topgallant sails & spanker. Saw plenty of porpoises. Middle part foggy, with light breeze from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. by S. Latter part calm. Saw several.

column10: Two unidentified ships
column12: Two humpbacks and two ships were sighted. A heavy squall forced the crew to reduce sail; the jib sheet parted and the jib split.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & very light breeze from the S. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. Saw 2 humpbacks & 2 ships. Employed in ship duty. Middle part thick overcast weather & light breeze from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. Latter part, at 4 P.M., a heavy squall. Furled everything but close-reefed main topsail & foresail. Parted jib sheet & split the jib. Blowing fresh from the northward. Ship lying to, heading west.

column12: A damaged jib was exchanged for another. A heavy gale forced the ship to lie to under reduced sail.
column13: First part of this day thick squally weather & strong breezes from the N.W. Ship steering S.W. under double-reefed topsail & foresail. At 8 A.M. sent in the jib to repair & sent out another one in place of it. Middle part heavy gale from the westward. Furled fore & mizzen topsails & foresail. Ship lying to under close-reefed main topsail, main spencer & fore topmast staysail. Latter part much the same. Saw nothing of note. Employed in ship duty.

column12: The bow boat was taken in and placed on the tryworks. The mizzen and main topsails were repaired as the gale moderated.
column13: First part of this day thick weather & strong gale from the N.W. Ship lying to under close-reefed main topsail & main topmast staysail & fore spencer. At 3 A.M. took in the bow boat & put her on the tryworks. Middle part more moderate. Set the foresail. Latter part pleasant weather & light breeze from the S.E. Ship heading S.W. by W. under all sail. Sent down the mizzen topsail to repair it. Employed in repairing the main topsail.

column10: Ship William Wirt of Fairhaven [noted as all on board well]
column12: New Year greeting recorded in the entry.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breezes from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. under all sail &c. At 2 A.M. sent up the main topsail & set it. This day we commence a new year. May it be a pleasant & prosperous one to all on board Ship William Wirt of Fairhaven. Middle part moderate breezes from the northward. Ship steering S.W. Latter part strong gale from the northward. Ship steering S.W. by S. under double topsail & three sails. No observation this day.

column12: The wind veered westward; the ship reduced sail and later sailed south.
column13: First part of this day thick overcast weather & strong breeze from the northward. Ship steering S.W. under double-reefed topsails & foresail. At 2 A.M. wind veered to the W.N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.S.W., under snug sail. Middle part pleasant. Latter part the same. Wind from the westward. Ship heading south under double-reefed topsails & courses & jib. Saw a finback & sunfish. Employed in ship duty.

column12: No observation was taken; crew performed ship duty and saw nothing of note.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate wind from the S.E. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. Employed in ship duty. Saw nothing of note. Middle part the same. Latter part thick squally weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering S.W. under topsails & courses & jib. Saw nothing. No observation this day.

column12: New main topgallant and fore topsails were bent; the ship tacked repeatedly and reduced sail.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the southward. Ship steering by the wind, heading W.N.W. At 3 A.M. bent a new main topgallant sail. At 6 A.M. bent a new fore topsail. At 7 A.M. tacked ship to the southward, wind about W.S.W. Middle part strong breeze from the W.S.W. Furled topgallant sail & jib & mainsail. Latter part, at 8 P.M., tacked to head W.N.W. At 11 P.M. tacked to the S.S.E. Winds variable, with pleasant weather.

column12: A finback was sighted after the ship changed from S.S.E. to S.W.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the W.S.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.S.E., with topsails, courses & jib set. Middle part much the same. Latter part pleasant. Wind from the N.W. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. Saw a finback.

column12: A finback was sighted; crew performed ship duty.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & light breeze from the N.W. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. Saw a finback. Middle part pleasant under snug sail. Latter part the same. Set all sail & ship steering S.W. Saw nothing of note. Employed in ship duty.

column10: One unidentified ship steering S.S.W.
column12: A new mizzen topsail and topgallant sail were bent during foggy and light-wind conditions.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & very light breeze from the N.E. Ship lying with main topsail to the mast. Middle part much the same, with thick fog. Latter part wind from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.S.W. under all sail. Saw a ship steering S.S.W. Employed in bending a new mizzen topsail & topgallant sail. Saw a sulphur-bottom.

column10: One unidentified ship off weather bow
column12: An unidentified ship remained in sight; the crew repaired the mainsail.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & light breeze from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. A ship in sight off the weather bow, steering S.S.W. Employed in ship duty. Middle part very light breeze. Latter part calm. Ship in sight. Employed in repairing the mainsail. Saw porpoises & grampuses.

column12: A boat chased grampuses but caught none; a strong gale forced the ship to lie to.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & light winds from the W.N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading south, under all sail. Saw grampuses. Lowered one boat in chase of them but caught none. Bent the mainsail. Middle part pleasant, with strong breeze from the S.S.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.E. At 12 M. called all hands to shorten sail. Blowing a strong gale from the S.S.W. Ship lying to under close-reefed main topsail & fore topmast staysail. Latter part more moderate. Set double-reefed topsail & foresail, heading S.E.

column12: Squalls and strong breezes moderated later; crew performed ship duty.
column13: First part of this day squally, with strong breeze from the S.S.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.E. by S., under double-reefed topsails & foresail. Middle part pleasant, with moderate breeze from the westward. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.S.W., under all sail. Latter part much the same. Saw porpoises. Employed in ship duty.

column12: Numerous finbacks and porpoises were sighted; the log says “but no whales.”
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the northward. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.S.W., under all sail. Saw finbacks & porpoises. Middle part thick. Latter part pleasant, with light winds from the westward. Ship steering S.W. by the wind. Saw plenty of finbacks & porpoises, but no whales. Employed in ship duty.

column12: Wind veered northward and strengthened, forcing the crew to reduce sail.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & very light breeze from the westward. Ship steering by the wind, heading south. Employed in ship duty. Middle part pleasant. Wind from the N.E. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. Latter part wind veered to the northward, blowing strong. Furled fore & mizzen topsails and all sail. Saw nothing.

column12: A strong gale forced the ship to lie to under reduced sail before conditions moderated.
column13: First part of this day thick overcast weather & strong gale from the S.W. Furled all sail except close-reefed main topsail & foresail. Ship lying to, heading S.E. At 1 A.M. wore ship to the westward. Middle part more moderate. Latter part pleasant, with moderate breeze from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. under all sail. Employed in ship duty. Saw nothing.

column10: Two ships; one brig — steering southward
column12: The waist boat was taken in and placed on the tryworks.
column13: First part of this day fine clear weather & strong breeze from the W.N.W. Ship steering S.W. At 5 A.M. furled two topsails, mainsail, & double-reefed the topsails. Fresh breeze & clear weather. Middle part much the same. Latter part pleasant. Wind from the W.S.W. Ship steering south under all sail. Saw two ships & a brig steering to the southward. At 6 P.M. took in the waist boat & put her on the tryworks. Employed in ship duty.

column10: Two ships; one brig — steering southward
column12: Coordinates are uncertain in the original; sail was reduced during strong winds and later reset.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the W.S.W. Ship steering south under all sail. Saw two ships & a brig steering southward. Employed in ship duty. Middle part strong breeze from the westward. Ship steering south. At 2 P.M. furled topgallant sail & double-reefed the topsails. Latter part more moderate. Wind west. Set topsails & main topgallant sail. Steering S. by E. Saw finbacks & porpoises.

column10: One topsail schooner
column12: Staten Land was sighted; its easternmost point bore S.E. by S., distant three leagues.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the westward. Ship steering S.E. under all topsails & main topgallant sail. Saw a topsail schooner steering south. Middle part very light wind from the northward. Ship steering S. by E. under all sail. Latter part calm. Staten Land in sight, the easternmost point bearing S.E. by S., distant 3 leagues. Ship steering E.S.E. with very light breeze from the N.N.W. A topsail schooner in sight.

column12: The middle of Staten Land bore S.E., distant eight leagues.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & very light breeze from the N.W. Ship steering E. by S. under all sail. The middle of Staten Land bearing S.E., distant 8 leagues. Middle part light wind from the N.N.W. Ship steering S.E.; very thick weather. Latter part wind from the westward, strong breeze. Furled topgallant sails & double-reefed the topsails. Ship heading south, with clear weather.

column12: Strong winds moderated later; the ship wore to the northwest.
column13: First part of this day fine clear weather & strong breeze from the westward. Ship steering by the wind, heading south, under double-reefed topsails, courses & jib. Middle part the same. Latter part more moderate. Wind from the W.S.W. At 4 P.M. wore ship to the N.W. Ship under single-reefed topsails, courses & jib.

column8: S. by W.; S.W. by W.
column12: No observation was taken; the ship continued under all sail after stronger winds early in the day.
column13: First part of this day pleasant clear weather & strong breeze from the westward. Ship steering by the wind, heading S. by W., under single-reefed topsails, courses, jib & spanker. Middle part pleasant, with moderate winds. Latter part pleasant, with wind from the northward. Ship steering S.W. by W. under all sail. Saw nothing of note. No observation this day.

column12: A strong gale forced the ship to lie to under close-reefed sail before conditions moderated.
column13: First part of this day fine, thick squally weather & strong breeze. At 2 A.M. wind veered to the westward. At 2¼ A.M. furled topgallant sail, double-reefed the topsails & furled the jib. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.S.W., with fresh breeze. Middle part strong gale from the westward. Furled fore & mizzen topsails. Ship lying to under close-reefed main topsail & foresail & fore topmast staysail & spencer. Latter part more moderate. Set single-reefed topsails, mainsail & jib. Wind west. Ship heading S.S.W.

column8: S.S.W.; S.W. by W.; W. by S.
column10: Two unidentified ships — steering S.S.W.
column12: Position recorded by dead reckoning; weather became thick after squalls and strong wind.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the westward. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.S.W., under single-reefed topsails, main topgallant sail, courses & jib. Two ships in sight, steering S.S.W. Middle part squally, with strong wind from the W.N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.W. by W., under double-reefed topsails, foresail & jib. Latter part more moderate. Wind N.N.W. Ship steering W. by S. under single-reefed topsails, foresail, jib & main topgallant sail. Thick weather.

column8: W.S.W.; lying to; N.W. by W.
column12: A heavy gale forced the ship to lie to under storm sail; sail was reset as conditions moderated.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant, thick overcast weather & strong breeze from the N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading W.S.W. At 1 A.M. furled main topgallant sail & mainsail. At 2 A.M. furled fore & mizzen topsails & foresail, and close-reefed the main topsail. Blowing a heavy gale from the N.W. Ship lying to under storm sail, heading W.S.W. Middle part more moderate. Set fore & mizzen topsails. Wind veered to the westward. At 8 P.M. tacked to the W.S.W., wind from the S.W. Latter part squally, with strong breeze from the S.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading N.W. by W., under double-reefed topsails & mainsail.

column10: Two ships; one topsail schooner
column12: Squalls, hail and strong winds moderated later; several vessels were sighted.
column13: First part of this day thick overcast weather & squally, with hail & strong breezes from the S.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading W.S.W., under double-reefed topsails & courses. Middle part more moderate. Set the jib & spanker. Latter part wore ship to the S.W. Wind W.N.W. Thick overcast, foggy weather with light breezes. Ship with all sail set. Two ships & a topsail schooner in sight. Saw finbacks.

column10: One topsail schooner; one unidentified ship steering N.W.
column12: No observation was taken; weather was very foggy.
column13: First part of this day thick overcast weather & light breeze from the W.N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.W., under all sail. One topsail schooner in sight. Middle part wind from the N.N.W. Ship steering W.S.W. under all sail. Very foggy. Latter part wind from the W.N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.W., under all sail. Saw a ship steering N.W. Employed in ship duty &c. No observation this day.

column12: Fog and rain were followed by a strong breeze; the main topgallant sail was furled.
column13: First part of this day foggy, with rain. Wind varying from the W.N.W. to N.N.W. Ship’s course W.S.W. under all sail. Middle part strong breeze from the N.E. Ship steering W. by S. At 6 A.M. furled main topgallant sail. Latter part wind the same. Ship steering west under topsails & courses.

column10: One fore-and-aft schooner — steering northward
column12: Strong winds forced the ship to lie to under reduced sail.
column13: First part of this day thick overcast weather & strong breezes from the N.N.W. Ship steering west. At 2 A.M. double-reefed the topsails & furled the jib. Middle part fresh breeze. Furled fore & mizzen topsails & mainsail. Ship lying to under close-reefed main topsail, main spencer & fore topmast staysail. Latter part wind veered to the W.N.W., with strong breeze. Set double-reefed topsails & foresail, heading S.W. Saw a fore-and-aft schooner steering to the northward.

column10: One barque
column12: A barque, porpoises and a finback were sighted.
column13: First part of this day thick weather & strong breeze from the W.S.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.W., under double-reefed topsails, courses & jib. One barque in sight. Middle part much the same. Latter part more moderate. Set all sail. Wind from the W.N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading S.W. Saw porpoises & a finback. Employed in ship duty.

column10: Two unidentified ships
column12: Calm conditions were followed by a light southwest breeze; two ships were sighted.
column13: First part of this day thick overcast weather & very light breeze from the N.W. Ship steering by the wind, heading west, under all sail. Saw nothing of note. Middle part calm. At 1 P.M. very light breeze from the S.W. Ship steering N.W. under all sail. Latter part wind the same, with moderate breeze. Saw plenty of porpoises & a finback. Two ships in sight.

column10: Two ships, then three ships — steering N.W.
column12: Multiple ships were sighted while the William Wirt sailed northwest.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the W.S.W. Ship steering N.W. under all sail. Two ships in sight, steering N.W. Middle part squally. Latter part pleasant. Wind from the S.W. by W. Ship steering N.W. by W. under all sail. Saw three ships steering N.W. Employed in ship duty.

column10: Seven vessels — steering N.W.
column12: Seven vessels were sighted sailing northwest; finbacks and grampuses were also seen.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the W.N.W. Ship steering N.W. by W. with all sail set. Saw finbacks. Middle part much the same. Latter part light wind from the W. by S. Ship steering N.W. with all sail set. Saw seven vessels, all steering N.W. Employed in ship duty. Saw finbacks & grampuses.

column8: N.W. by N.; N. by W.; N.N.W.
column10: Ship Seine — New Bedford; six other ships
column12: Spoke the New Bedford ship Seine, Captain Seabury, eight months out with 80 barrels of sperm oil.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the westward. Ship steering N.W. by N. under all sail. Saw seven sail of vessels, all steering N.W. by N. At 7 A.M. spoke Ship Seine of New Bedford, Captain Seabury, eight months out, with 80 barrels of sperm oil. Middle part pleasant, steering N. by W. Latter part pleasant. Ship under all sail, steering N.N.W. At 10 P.M. spoke Ship Seine of New Bedford. Six ships in sight, steering N.N.W. Saw porpoises &c.

column10: Three ships; one brig — steering N.N.W.
column12: Four vessels were sighted steering N.N.W.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Saw three ships & one brig steering N.N.W. Middle part the same. Latter part very pleasant. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Employed in ship duty.

column10: Ship Seine; four sail initially; two other ships later
column12: The Seine remained in sight with several other vessels; numerous finbacks and porpoises were seen.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Four sail in sight. Middle part pleasant. Latter part very pleasant. Wind from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Ship Seine in sight & two other ships. Saw plenty of finbacks & porpoises. Employed in ship duty.

column10: Ship Seine
column12: Crew worked on royal and studding-sail rigging; the writer added “Hope to soon” after reporting no sightings.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Ship Seine in sight. Middle part pleasant. Latter part wind from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Employed in bending the main royal mast & fore topmast studding-sail boom. Saw nothing of note. Hope to soon.

column12: Crew sent up royal yards and masts and fitted the flying-jib boom.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Employed in sending up main royal yard & sail. Middle part the same. Latter part very pleasant, with light wind from the S.S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Saw finbacks & porpoises. Employed in sending up fore & mizzen royal masts & fitting flying-jib boom.

column10: Ship Seine
column12: The Seine remained in sight; the crew sent out the flying-jib boom.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Employed in ship duty. Saw finbacks. Ship Seine still in sight. Middle part much the same. Latter part wind S.S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. Sent out flying-jib boom.

column10: Ship Seine
column12: The Seine remained in sight while the crew set up the head rigging.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Ship Seine in sight. Middle part much the same. Latter part wind from the S.E. by S. Ship steering N. by W. under all sail. Saw finbacks & porpoises. Employed in ship duty & in setting up the head rigging. Ship Seine in sight.

column10: Ship Line — New Bedford; Captain Landis
column12: Spoke and parted company with a New Bedford ship whose name and captain are uncertain in the manuscript.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N. by W. under all sail. At 6 A.M. spoke Ship Line of New Bedford, Captain Landis. At 6 A.M. parted company. Middle part pleasant. Latter part very pleasant. Wind from the S.E. Ship steering N. by W. under all sail. Employed in setting up the lower rigging, fore & aft. Saw a few birds &c. End.

column10: Ship Constitution — Nantucket, Capt. Bunker; Ship Sharon — Fairhaven, Capt. Rule; Ship Hector — Capt. Slocum
column12: Más Afuera sighted. Constitution reported 500 barrels sperm oil; Sharon 1,100; Hector 200.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. by E. Ship steering north under all sail. Employed in setting up the rigging & other small jobs. Middle part pleasant. Latter part the same. At 5 P.M. the island of Masafuero in sight, bearing N.W., distant 15 leagues. At 10 P.M. spoke Ship Constitution, Captain Bunker, 20 months from Nantucket, 500 barrels sperm oil. At 10½ P.M. spoke Ship Sharon, Captain Rule, 31 months from Fairhaven, 1,100 barrels sperm oil. At 11 P.M. spoke Ship Hector, Captain Slocum, 28 months out, 200 barrels sperm oil. At 12 parted company with them all & steered N.W.

column10: Ship Spartan — Nantucket, 20 months out
column12: Más Afuera bore N.E., closing from five to two leagues; a boat went ashore and returned with fish.
column13: First part of this day squally, with rain. Masafuero bearing N.E., distant 5 leagues. Middle part pleasant. At 8 A.M. furled topgallant sail & hauled main topsail to the mast. Latter part steering in for the land. At 8 P.M. the boat went on shore fishing. At midnight returned with a mess of fish. Spoke Ship Spartan of Nantucket, 20 months out. Masafuero bearing N.E., distant 2 leagues.

column10: Ship Staten — Nantucket
column12: Parted company with the Staten at 10 A.M.; the initial course afterward is uncertain.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the south. In company with Ship Staten of Nantucket. At 10 A.M. parted company with her and steered S.E. under all sail. At 4 P.M. strong breeze from the S.E. Ship steering north under all sail. Saw nothing of note. Hope to soon.

column12: The ship continued north under all sail and saw nothing of note.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & strong breeze from the S.E. by S. Ship steering north under all sail. Middle part the same. Latter part wind S.E. Ship steering north under all sail. Saw nothing of note. Employed in ship duty.

column12: Finbacks and porpoises were seen during the latter part of the day.
column13: First part of these twenty-four hours fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N. by E. under all sail. Saw nothing of note. Middle part pleasant. Latter part wind from the south. Ship steering N. by E. under all sail. Saw finbacks & porpoises. Employed in ship duty &c.

column8: N. by E.; N. by W.
column12: Finbacks and grampuses were sighted.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the south. Ship steering N. by E. under all sail. Saw finbacks. Employed in ship duty. Middle part much the same. Latter part very light breeze from the southward. Ship steering N. by W. under all sail. Saw finbacks & grampuses. Employed in ship duty.

column12: Finbacks and grampuses were sighted as the ship continued northward.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the southward. Ship steering N. by W. under all sail. Employed in ship duty. Middle part much the same. Latter part very pleasant, with very light breeze from the S.E. by E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Employed in ship duty. Saw finbacks & grampuses.

column12: The writer hoped to see whales before many days had passed.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & light breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N.W. by N. under all sail. Saw nothing of note. Employed in ship duty. Middle part much the same. Latter part wind from the S.E. Ship steering N.W. by N. under all sail. Saw nothing of note. Employed in ship duty. Hope to see whales before many days are passed.

column12: A finback was sighted in both the first and latter parts of the day.
column13: First part of this day fine pleasant weather & moderate breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Saw a finback. Middle part pleasant. Latter part very light breeze from the S.E. Ship steering N.N.W. under all sail. Saw a finback.
